claims.challenge_claim: The paper proves DPO-RLHF equivalence is conditional on the RLHF-optimal policy preferring human-preferred responses (Section 3).
limitations: Evaluated on finite two-response preference model without neural network parametrization.
Only the challenge can issue official verdict labels.
claims.summary: Evaluated DPO-RLHF equivalence across 112 finite preference cases; population cross-entropy stationary point matches RLHF optimum, but one-sided DPO loss has no finite minimum.

claims.challenge_claim: When the equivalence assumption fails, DPO optimizes relative advantage over the reference policy rather than absolute human-preference alignment (Section 3).
limitations: Evaluated on finite two-response preference model without neural network parametrization.
Only the challenge can issue official verdict labels.
claims.summary: Evaluated 75 preference shifts where DPO improves relative log-likelihood advantage over reference policy without achieving absolute preference alignment.

claims.challenge_claim: The paper characterizes undesirable solution spaces in which policies reduce DPO loss while preferring dispreferred responses (Section 3).
limitations: Evaluated on finite two-response preference model without neural network parametrization.
Only the challenge can issue official verdict labels.
claims.summary: Identified concrete witness pairs where DPO loss decreases while the model policy continues to prefer the dispreferred response.

claims.challenge_claim: Constrained Preference Optimization augments RLHF with constraints and derives a stationary DPO-like loss with an adaptive reference-based margin (Section 4.3).
limitations: Evaluated on finite two-response preference model without neural network parametrization.
Only the challenge can issue official verdict labels.
claims.summary: Audited 180 CPO grid cases; exact constrained RLHF objective is unbounded for gamma > 0 at preferred boundary, while Equation 17 reference-margin substitution yields a stationary DPO-like loss.

claims.challenge_claim: The paper gives a soft-margin ranking interpretation showing DPO can implement margin ranking with potentially negative targets (Section 5).
limitations: Evaluated on finite two-response preference model without neural network parametrization.
Only the challenge can issue official verdict labels.
claims.summary: Verified convergence of scaled DPO loss to literal hinge loss across 150 cases as beta increases, confirming soft-margin ranking interpretation with negative target margins.

claims.challenge_claim: Experiments on standard benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance for CPO (Section 6).
limitations: Advertised repository visitworld123/CPO was unavailable during assessment.
GPU training and benchmark evaluation are out of finite CPU reproduction scope.
claims.summary: Benchmark SOTA performance claim was not reproduced.
